catalogue_requests.reason: cap.motion.joint_position.v1 fixes joint_positions to radians and a joint order, while this stage addresses X and Y in micrometres and R in degrees (docs/DESIGN.md:53-58) and the clone states no conversion of those native units to radians; cap.motion.cartesian_pose.v1 binds robot.arm and takes millimetres, not this controller's rotation axis. The extension carries the native engineering units.
catalogue_requests.summary: Move the ZC300 XYR stage to an absolute X/Y/R position in micrometres and degrees, then wait until the controller reports all axes stopped.

notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/labs/lewbert__talos-2d-transfer --backend fake: G1 to G9 pass and check-report.json has no finding, warning or error. Evidence is contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level. No hardware was attached, the hardware backend and native.py were never imported or run, no upstream clone code was imported or executed, and nothing was installed. The package is model-authored (driver.lock.json authored_by kind model, model_id deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017, run_id helper-wave-2-005); reviewed_by is null, no human reviewed or tested anything, and no hardware run is claimed. This is an R2 package: the loader refuses the hardware backend of an unreviewed model-written package until a human signs reviewed_by, and the model claims no protection beyond that.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card's PythonObjectDriver helper is not used. This is a direct Driver over the card's entry symbol talos.hal.devices.zolix:ZolixXYRStage (talos/hal/devices/zolix.py:99) with a native.py factory, because the upstream assembles every Modbus RTU frame from an opcode, axis selector, direction and exact register count (talos/hal/devices/zolix.py:47-56, 330-346) and its absolute move is composed from validated fixed-length moves and then polled to rest. A one-call object binding cannot preserve that wire form or the two-step move. The card decision direct-driver and the entry symbol are unchanged.

Interface: reads x_um, y_um, r_deg (the controller's own position readback, already in micrometres and degrees through the configured scale), moving, the controller status emergency-stop bit, and the alarm bit; the extension x-cap.lewbert.stage_move_abs.v1 for an absolute X/Y/R move that waits for rest; cap.motion.stop.v1 for the native stop, also the safe-state action; an interlock that blocks the move while the controller reports the emergency-stop input or an axis alarm. Limits: the X, Y and R travel ranges are Limit.operator_required because no text file of the clone states the travel of this stage (docs/DESIGN.md:45-58 gives the register map and the 0.625 micrometre/pulse and 0.00125 degree/pulse scale but no end stops); site-limits.example.json is only a narrow example overlay, not a device bound. Every move is refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET until the site supplies site-limits.json. The constructor's port, pulse scale, speed and stop mode are deployment options of native.py, not facts or limits of this bench.

Stop path and its limits: the upstream stop() sends the configured stop opcode to all axes, verifies with a bounded status poll, escalates to the immediate stop and verifies again, and never raises (talos/hal/devices/zolix.py:347-365). Its _wait_stopped helper treats a failed status read as stopped (talos/hal/devices/zolix.py:367-381), so the driver's safe-state action makes its own fresh status read and reports stopped from it; if that read raises, the safe-state action fails rather than claiming quiescence. There is no re-enable or re-arm step in the upstream driver and no new native session; an accepted operator reset only releases the runtime latch. No line of the clone documents a separate physical e-stop switch, an e-stop wiring diagram or a safety-rated channel, so estop_physical_ref is not set and the package claims only the safe_state=True action for SAFE-045. The physical e-stop, if one exists, stays authoritative; OpenMHS is not a safety certification.

The clone has no recorded traffic and no Zolix simulator used by this package. fake.py is an analytic in-memory stand-in at the level of the upstream ZolixXYRStage methods, uses only method names that exist on that class (gate G7), opens no port, and marks every start value and its fixed 0.08 s placeholder move time as test data. It is not a recording, not the upstream simulator, and its timing is not the [...]

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the direct Driver over ZolixXYRStage line by line against zolix.py, its models and codec, docs/DESIGN.md and the upstream tests: the stop is source-backed (the configured stop opcode to all axes, polled and escalated to the immediate stop, zolix.py:347-384), the travel inputs are rightly operator_required, no @reset, re-enable or terminal declaration exists or is needed (the stop writes no enable register), and native.py only builds the class and calls connect(). Defect: the safe-state action returned stopped false as a completed result when its fresh status read still showed motion, which the runtime counts as the safe state reached (a probe whose fake ignored the stop got a completed e-stop with safe_state_achieved true while the stage moved); it now fails MHS.SAFETY.SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED (latch held) and a new test fails on the author's version. Also corrected: facts saying more than their lines (bit 9 off-range, a 'so' inference, the lock's use), a stopped output claiming a limit-switch check, and facts.md denying the upstream simulator twin and naming none of the bench's other devices; facts were added (connect()'s enable and acceleration writes, the constructor defaults, move_rel_um's lock scope, session-relative coordinates). Changed driver.py, test_driver.py (unconfirmed-stop and e-stop-bit interlock cases), fake.py (refuses a move while its e-stop bit is set; gaps stated), native.py (docstring) and facts.md, regenerating reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json; gate and strict collector pass, digest unchanged (sha256:f425f3ccf4f6cce9a2416f8064518addae606a11fc8569240a3c8455a06115aa). Stale author text: the RESULT.json notes say the upstream has no re-enable or re-arm step (connect() enables the axes) and that the safe-state action reports stopped from its read (it now fails while an axis moves). For the human reviewer: Motorised XYR sample stage (R2). The upstream stop swallows every error, so only the package's fresh status read confirms the stop, and that read trusts the motion-state words (1 = moving, zolix.py:58, 399): check them against the ZC300 manual. Opening the hardware backend writes each axis's enable register and acceleration (accel_pps2, default 10_000_000) unasked. The site envelope bounds targets in the controller's position frame, which the README calls session-relative (README.md:74-75) and this package cannot home. After a serial error the upstream marks itself disconnected (zolix.py:498-500) and nothing reconnects it: every later stop fails SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED until the endpoint restarts. A move ending on an alarm, the e-stop bit or its deadline sends no stop; limit switches are not checked. An escalating stop can outlast the 1000 ms default e-stop budget (reported unreached, then confirmed by the retry). No physical e-stop or safety-rated channel is documented. Unused upstream defect: check_estop catches DeviceError, never imported (zolix.py:433-437).

MODEL REVIEW (claude-sonnet-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Adversarial verification of the claude-opus-5-5 review (fix) by a different model (the user chose Claude Sonnet as the different model, 2026-11-04): the verifier agreed and found no blocker or major. No blocker or major found. I re-ran the gate (G1-G9 pass, digest sha256:f425f3cc... unchanged) and `collect.py --strict` (PASS, 0 with warnings). `show_refs.py` reports 17 citations and 0 bad. I read every cited range against the clone. They support the Facts as written, including the narrowed stop and `_wait_stopped` Facts and the connect-time enable and acceleration writes (zolix.py:136-164). The stop is source-backed. `stop_motion` calls the native stop and then makes a fresh status read. It raises `MHS.SAFETY.SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED` if an axis still moves or if the read fails. That closes the hole where `_wait_stopped` treats a failed read as stopped. The travel inputs are `operator_required`, there is no `@reset` or re-enable, and R2 fits a motorised stage.
